speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Therefore, I convened this COI because the Government wanted a robust and transparent inquiry that would get to the bottom of this cyberattack and, in particular, the COI was asked to, firstly, establish the events and contributing factors and evaluate the incident response by the Integrated Healthcare Information Systems Private Limited (IHiS) and SingHealth.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And secondly, to recommend measures to safeguard public sector information technology (IT) systems that contain large databases of personal data against similar cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Committee conducted a rigorous and comprehensive inquiry over five months.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They examined testimonies from 37 witnesses, including local and foreign experts, as well as 26 written representations from members of the public, professional associations, organisations and companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The COI conducted 22 days of hearings which were opened to the public except when there were implications for national security or patient confidentiality.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The COI also released a public version of the report on 10 January 2019 which my Ministry has distributed to Members of this House.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The public report contains all recommendations and material findings from the full COI report.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It only excludes highly sensitive information heard by the COI in closed-door sessions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: At this juncture, on behalf of the Government, I would like to place on record our deep gratitude to the Committee for its hard work in undertaking a robust and transparent inquiry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would also like to thank the Attorney-General's Chambers, investigators from the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), and the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) officers who supported the COI, witnesses who gave evidence, as well as organisations, professionals and members of the public who contributed their views and suggestions in the course of the Inquiry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IHiS and SingHealth should have been better prepared and more robust in their actions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If they had done so, the cyberattack could have been limited or even stopped.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, the COI found significant shortcomings at the staff level.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IHiS staff did not have adequate cybersecurity awareness, training and resources to appreciate the security implications of their observations and to respond effectively to the attack.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Also, certain IHiS staff holding key roles in IT security incident response and reporting failed to take appropriate or timely action, even when there were clear signs of an ongoing attack.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: However, and this is noteworthy, the COI also commended specific IHiS IT administrators who were vigilant, noticed the suspicious activities and took the initiative to follow up.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, the COI found a number of vulnerabilities, weaknesses and misconfigurations at the technical level in the SingHealth network and database system which allowed the attacker to obtain and exfiltrate the data.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Many of these could have been remedied before the attack.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Third, the COI observed that although SingHealth was ultimately responsible, it had no management line of sight with regard to the assessment of the cybersecurity risks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SingHealth lacked the necessary expertise and resources and was wholly dependent on IHiS, even at the management level.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI, having heard evidence from CSA, also established that the cyberattack was the work of a skilled and sophisticated actor bearing the characteristics of an APT group.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This finding was corroborated by international expert witnesses.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: An APT group is a class of cyberattackers, typically state-linked, who conduct extended cyber campaigns to steal information or disrupt operations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI found that the attacker was well-resourced and had used advanced techniques and tools to target the SingHealth patient database and illegally exfiltrate patient data.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The attacker was persistent, evaded detection for a long time and even re-entered the network after being detected.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Appropriate action has been taken, and we know the identity of the attacker.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But for national security reasons, I will not comment further.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The detailed evidence for all of the COI's findings are in the public report, but it does not include highly sensitive information – pertaining to SingHealth's network architecture, technical vulnerabilities exploited in the attack, and the identity of the attacker – which is only in the classified COI report.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The recommendations fall into four broad categories – People, Process, Technology and Partnerships.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On People, the COI notes that frontend users are often the weakest link targeted by attackers, and that it is line staff who are often the first to notice a security incident and respond.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Hence, the recommendations include enhancing cyber hygiene practices, building a culture of cybersecurity across the entire organisation, and ensuring that IT staff are well-trained and equipped to respond to cybersecurity incidents.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI also calls for strong institutional Processes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In incident response, for example, there should be clear plans and standard operating procedures (SOPs) and regular exercises with realistic scenarios to test their effectiveness.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There should also be regular and comprehensive checks to identify vulnerabilities and high-risk areas, accompanied by audit and compliance checks, to ensure that the identified gaps have been plugged.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On Technology, the COI has proposed various measures to strengthen cybersecurity to better prevent, detect and respond to future attacks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These include stronger encryption for data, heightened monitoring of database activity, and an integrated system to aggregate and analyse threat information in real-time and rapidly isolate and contain the infected system.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI has highlighted the need to build up collective security over our systems, given that Singapore is highly connected and a high-value target.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This can be achieved by strengthening Partnerships between the Government, industry and international partners, in areas, such as threat intelligence sharing.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI has emphasised that, ultimately, cybersecurity must be an integral part of a broader risk management framework and cannot be treated merely as a technical matter.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Organisations need to strike a balance between security considerations, operational requirements and cost, and these tradeoffs and decisions must be made at the Board and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) level, and not just by the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and technical staff.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I will now elaborate on the Government’s efforts, ongoing and in response to the COI report, to strengthen cybersecurity at both the national level and across the public sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong will cover the public healthcare sector’s efforts.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Government’s approach to cybersecurity is underpinned by two key principles that have also been highlighted by the COI.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, we adopt a "defence-in-depth" strategy, with multiple layers of cyber defences to impede an attacker.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These layers of defence cascade from the perimeter to within our systems, as we recognise that a sophisticated and determined attacker, given enough time and resources, may find a way through.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is why we also have capabilities in our layered defence that enable swift detection of a breach and a decisive response.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, we seek to enhance our system defences by strengthening our people, processes and technology.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our aim is not only to monitor and respond robustly to an incident, but also to ensure a quick recovery and resilience in our system.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI emphasised that the battle against today’s cyber threats must be based on networked defence across organisations and sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The COI also recognised the Government’s commitment to such collective security, by establishing CSA to coordinate our national cybersecurity efforts.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA leads our national-level response to the cyber threat, including by reinforcing cybersecurity in all CII sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Immediately after the cyberattack, and even as the COI proceedings were underway, CSA instructed all CII sectors to strengthen network security by taking additional prescribed measures, such as removing non-essential connections to unsecured external networks and implementing uni-directional gateways like data diodes to prevent data leakage.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA also accelerated the implementation of the Cybersecurity Act, which provides the legislative framework for the oversight and maintenance of national cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All CII owners must now comply with their obligations under the Act.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These include adhering to essential cybersecurity measures set by CSA through the Cybersecurity Code of Practice, reporting cyber incidents to CSA within prescribed timeframes, and conducting regular risk assessments and audits of their CIIs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In addition, CSA also instructed all CII owners through their sector leads to conduct thorough internal reviews of their cybersecurity posture against the gaps identified during the COI hearings.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These included reviews of their people, process and technology measures, such as mandating cybersecurity training and awareness programmes, establishing a robust patch management process and implementing access management solutions to manage privileged administrator accounts.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA has directed CII owners to implement plans to close any identified gaps and report the results.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: CSA will continue to actively work with the sector leads and CII owners to reinforce their cyber defences and cyber resilience and safeguard the cybersecurity of our systems and networks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I now turn to the cybersecurity of public sector systems, which is a key enabler for our Smart Nation initiatives to improve public services for our citizens and businesses.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Smart Nation and Digital Government Group (SNDGG) had already started enhancing the cybersecurity of Government systems before the cyberattack.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, SNDGG and CSA reviewed the Government’s cybersecurity posture, and introduced additional measures on critical Government systems to enable us to detect and respond more quickly to cybersecurity threats.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The findings and recommendations of the COI give added impetus to our efforts to continuously review and enhance the cybersecurity of Government systems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In particular, the findings reaffirmed the "defence-in-depth" approach that the public sector had adopted towards cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The public sector will also continue to strengthen our defences on all fronts – people, process, technology and partnerships – as informed by the COI recommendations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In terms of people and processes, SNDGG will strengthen existing processes to prevent lapses and heighten vigilance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The public sector will use technology even more to support its IT staff and automate cybersecurity tasks, such as patch management, so as to carry out these tasks more reliably.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SNDGG will further tighten internal checks and enhance security audits, for example, by increasing their frequency.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will also instil a stronger cybersecurity culture across the Public Service.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This will be done by conducting more exercises to sharpen our officers' readiness and train all public servants in cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Above all, we expect our officers at all levels to be aware of their responsibilities, to be accountable for their actions, and to perform their duties to the best of their ability.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the technical front, SNDGG will continue to shore up defences at the perimeter of Government systems, while introducing measures to better detect and respond to intrusions within our systems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Beyond the measures implemented during the pause in the rollout of new Government systems, such as monitoring critical Government databases, SNDGG is also looking into improving the architecture of Government systems to enable more extensive monitoring and detection of abnormal activities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We also recognise that the Government cannot strengthen its cybersecurity alone.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, the Government will enlist the expertise of the larger cybersecurity community, including ethical hackers, to help us surface and detect vulnerabilities in our information and communication technologies (ICT) systems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This will help us draw in a wide range of expertise to help identify cyber blind spots and benchmark our defences against skilled global hackers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In terms of tracking the follow-up, CSA will oversee the follow-up on the COI's recommendations across all CII sectors, which includes the public sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To do this, CSA will work through the sector leads of the 11 CII sectors who are responsible to monitor implementation for their respective sectors and to report progress to CSA as the national cybersecurity authority.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SNDGG, as sector lead for the Government sector, will monitor implementation for Government systems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will then track overall progress via regular updates at the relevant Ministerial committees.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) has also completed its investigations of the data breach incident.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The measures recommended by the COI will help us defend ourselves better against malicious cyber activities, including from international attackers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This was not the first instance where we were targeted and it will not be the last.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our networks are continually probed for weaknesses and regularly attacked.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: A cyberattack of the scale and sophistication that was launched against SingHealth could also be mounted on any one of our major IT systems, threatening the safety and security of Singapore and Singaporeans, which are of paramount importance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singapore is firmly committed to the establishment of a rules-based international order in cyberspace.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We condemn all malicious cyber activity that seeks to undermine the integrity of the international political and economic system and violates the norms of behaviour in cyberspace as set out in the 2015 United Nations (UN) Group of Governmental Experts consensus report.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This includes the cyber-enabled theft of sensitive data.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Such activities can have a disruptive impact on Singapore and internationally in our highly interconnected world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singapore has consistently advocated that the international community come together to build consensus and develop a rules- and norms-based international order in cyberspace, a cyberspace that fosters trust and confidence, and one where its users can remain safe and secure.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is consistent with Singapore's fundamental stand that a rules-based multilateral system is indispensable to secure peace and stability in the international arena.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To this end, Singapore has been actively hosting and supporting regional and international discussions and cybersecurity programmes aimed at building consensus on the rules of behaviour in cyberspace.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singapore stands ready to work with all parties toward closer international cooperation in the cyber and digital sphere.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The findings and recommendations of the COI into the SingHealth cyberattack have helped to sharpen our focus and given further impetus to our efforts to secure our systems and databases, especially against a sophisticated cyberattacker.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But there is no permanent fix nor absolute cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is a constant battle against cunning adversaries with advanced capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we cannot let incidents like this derail our Smart Nation initiatives that can enhance our economic competitiveness and deliver better public services for the benefit of our citizens.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will do our utmost to strengthen Singapore's cyber defence capabilities and prevent cybersecurity breaches.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: However, if a breach occurs despite our best efforts, we must have the capability to detect it quickly and respond robustly to minimise the damage.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our people must stay resilient in the face of such a continuing threat while doing their part for our cyber defence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will learn from this incident, emerge stronger and uphold the trust of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Minister of Health will be making a related Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarification on both Statements after this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The healthcare system’s foremost priority is our patients' well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This encompasses not just safe and effective care, but also the protection of their personal data.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We, the healthcare family, have a responsibility to our patients to ensure both these aspects.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Once again, I apologise to our patients on behalf of our healthcare family.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Iswaran has provided a summary of the COI’s findings and recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with the COI that we were lacking in several areas.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of our IT personnel did not have sufficient levels of cybersecurity awareness, training and resources to respond to the attack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Certain staff with key roles in IT security incident response failed to take essential actions, resulting in missed opportunities to prevent the attack or minimise its impact.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There were vulnerabilities in our IT system that were exploited by the attacker.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Examples include servers that were not adequately secured against unauthorised access, and weak passwords and administrator account controls.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There were gaps in the management of IT assets, compliance with security policies, as well as inadequate remediation of known system vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The public healthcare family needs to do much better.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These have been touched on by Minister Iswaran.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: So, I will not go through in detail.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I will instead focus on the healthcare family’s responses and follow-up actions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The COI findings and recommendations will play an important role in guiding our actions and our cybersecurity direction going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ATP identifies threats based on the techniques used by more advanced threat actors and is better able to detect customised hacking tools designed to bypass conventional defences; and (f) IHiS has also improved its incident response processes and SOPs, with clearer channels of reporting and escalation criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Subsequently, in November 2018, IHiS announced further measures which are being implemented progressively across public healthcare agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) has been implemented for the SingHealth electronic medical record database.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: DAM provides more comprehensive alerts and blocks database queries from unauthorised sources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IHiS has strengthened the security of domain controllers, by limiting login access and requiring two-factor authentication for administrative access.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In assessing and developing these measures, IHiS had benefited from the inputs and advice of CSA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Parallel measures were also taken by SingHealth in patient engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include all patients who visited SingHealth Specialist Outpatient Clinics and polyclinics from the start of 2015 to the attack, including those whose data were not accessed, in order to reassure them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: SingHealth has since also taken steps to improve the accuracy of patients’ contact information for better patient engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, it has identified patients without valid contact details so that staff can update the patients’ contact details at their next visit.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since November 2018, SingHealth has been sending short message service (SMS) to all patients on the day of their outpatient appointments to remind them to approach counter staff to update contact details if there are any changes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: SingHealth will be sharing their learning points with the other clusters and we will be making similar improvements across public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On our part, MOH has initiated independent security reviews on key public healthcare IT systems to identify vulnerabilities and recommend measures to address them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At a broader systemic level, MOH has appointed a Cybersecurity Advisory Committee (CAC) to conduct a horizontal review of the cybersecurity governance structures and processes across the public healthcare clusters and IHiS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Committee is chaired by Prof Tan Chorh Chuan and comprises industry experts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is supported by independent consultants from KPMG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Committee has just submitted an interim update to me on the findings and recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will be studying these closely and will start pursuing key interim proposals even as the Committee continues its work.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Beyond our own plans and efforts, the COI report has provided us valuable inputs and useful recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will follow up on them, but I will highlight our thinking and plans in response to some of the key recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The COI has recommended that we enhance our security structure and readiness across IHiS and the public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We need to better organise and govern our cybersecurity oversight and efforts and give cybersecurity considerations more weight in decision-making.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is an important area that is also being reviewed by the CAC I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It also highlighted the need to elevate cybersecurity roles and functions to strengthen management oversight over cybersecurity, supported with the appropriate resources and expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH agrees and we will implement the following organisational changes in line with these guiding principles.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the Ministry, the MOH Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is currently also the Director of Cyber Security Governance at IHiS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The MOH CISO office will be the cybersecurity sector lead for the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will coordinate efforts to protect the CII in the healthcare sector and ensure that the sector fulfils its regulatory obligations under the Cybersecurity Act.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For its part, IHiS will have its own separate Director of Cyber Security Governance.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the clusters, the cluster Group Chief Information Officer (GCIO) office will now be made fully accountable to the respective cluster management and Boards.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The GCIO office will be adequately resourced to carry out its roles.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Together, these moves will strengthen oversight and minimise potential conflicts of interest between cybersecurity and operational demands.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, we will put in place a cybersecurity model with multiple lines of defence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The COI has recommended that the public healthcare sector review our cyber stack for adequacy in defending and responding to advanced threats and subject the systems to tighter control and monitoring.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The CAC, too, has highlighted the need for a more robust "Three Lines of Defence" model.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We agree and we will establish a more robust "Three Lines of Defence" structure within public healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The first line comprises units and personnel who develop, deliver and operate the IT systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will strengthen the IT delivery group to better integrate cybersecurity into IT delivery initiatives, improve the management of network security, and increase emphasis on security architecture and monitoring.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The strengthened group will have independent oversight of cybersecurity implementation, compliance and risk management, and will oversee incident reporting and management.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will ensure that cybersecurity is managed at the senior management level, and an appropriate balance is struck between service delivery and cybersecurity considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The third line of defence comprises checks and assurances independent of IHiS and our healthcare clusters, and independent of the first two lines of defence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH Holdings Group Internal Audit will continue to play this role.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also intend to commission and tap on independent third parties where appropriate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These changes will make our public healthcare system more resilient and robust against emerging and evolving cyber threats.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, we will improve our staff’s cybersecurity awareness and capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The COI has made several recommendations in this area.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We agree that the "people" element is foundational and critical to our cyber defences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Every user needs to be trained and equipped to understand the important role that they play in cyber defence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, to raise the competence of our security incident response personnel, IHiS will engage specialist providers to conduct realistic hands-on "Cyber Range" simulation training starting this year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will augment the classroom discussion-style table-top exercises currently conducted for security incident response personnel.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also tap on the expertise of the wider cybersecurity community to test our systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IHiS intends to learn from GovTech's bug bounty and vulnerability disclosure programmes and start similar efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will be a further step to ensure that our systems are tested, our people are ready to deal with new challenges, and our processes are robust.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Next, we will pilot a tiered model of Internet access.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In its report, the COI has recommended that an Internet access strategy which minimises exposure to external threats should be implemented.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Following the cyberattack, temporary ISS was implemented across our public healthcare sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This was a necessary precaution as suspicious activity continued to be observed on the SingHealth systems, even after initial containment actions were taken.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I had mentioned in my previous statement in this House that we would study the impact of ISS, determine whether ISS can be kept as a permanent measure and if long-term mitigation solutions can be developed to overcome the operational challenges arising from ISS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While the implementation of ISS was necessary, it has, indeed, posed challenges in the provision of patient care in some areas, such as emergency care, decision support for prescriptions and treatments, access to patient education resources and booking of clinical appointments.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ISS also caused delays to frontline patient management and backend administrative tasks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Research and education initiatives in the public healthcare institutions have also been impacted by ISS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ISS impacted the functionality of Internet-based video conferencing software used to conduct tele-consultation with the National Neuroscience Institute for suspected stroke patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This software was used by some of our hospitals which do not have inhouse specialist neurology capabilities as timely diagnosis is critical for stroke cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A dedicated leased line to support high resolution video conferencing had to be provided to overcome this challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Where possible, we have put in place fixes and workarounds like this to reduce the impact to patients and healthcare staff.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we can continue to operate on this current model of ISS, we have also been looking for longer-term solutions that are more efficient and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also need a solution that will allow us to implement new models of care in the future, such as telemedicine, that leverage the Internet to improve patient care and services in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is why we have been experimenting with a "Virtual Browser" solution, even before the cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A "Virtual Browser" allows access to the Internet through strictly controlled and monitored client servers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we imagine loading a webpage or downloading a file from the Internet to be like receiving a letter, the client server is like a decontamination room where the letter is opened and only a picture is taken and sent to the recipient.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The recipient reads the letter only via the picture that was taken and does not touch the letter itself.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This process makes things safer for the recipient as malicious material or hidden messages are left behind in the decontamination room.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Although such a solution does not fully eliminate cybersecurity risks, it reduces the attack surface significantly, while minimising impact on service efficiency and patient care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our earlier trial conducted at the healthcare clusters has shown that a "Virtual Browser" is technically feasible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our next step will be to run a pilot in an operational environment across different settings and healthcare roles, so as to assess its effectiveness in meeting both operational and cybersecurity needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If the Virtual Browser is found to be effective, we envisage putting in place a tiered model of Internet access among our healthcare staff in the longer term.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For some job roles, Internet access would not be required.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, administrative staff handling certain backend tasks, may not need Internet access for their routine work, and these staff will not be provided Internet access.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For a number of job roles, Internet access is required but can be managed through the use of separate Internet and non-Internet facing devices.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This would likely be the case for the majority.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: ISS will remain for this group and they will have access to the Internet via a separate device.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will further improve our current arrangements so as to make it more convenient for this group of users.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For some, access to the Internet and intranet systems on the same device is essential.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This group could include clinicians who need to access the Internet for information from clinical reference databases and match them urgently against patients’ electronic medical records, such as information on new and complex drugs or obscure toxins.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Virtual Browser may be the best solution for this group.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Virtual Browsers will be deployed in selected job functions at selected departments and clinics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of the job roles participating in the pilot include frontline pharmacists and emergency department clinicians.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Apart from this small group of pilot Virtual Browser users, all other public healthcare staff will remain on ISS for now.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will work closely with CSA to assess the cybersecurity adequacy of the solution.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also evaluate the effectiveness of the Virtual Browser.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will enable us to make a more considered decision on our Internet access model in public healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Earlier, I mentioned that we have also started independent security reviews of other key public healthcare IT systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One such system being reviewed is the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These cover technical architecture design and existing cybersecurity measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, we are completing a series of penetration tests to uncover any security vulnerabilities against cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we conduct the reviews, IHiS will implement further enhancements to strengthen cybersecurity of the NEHR system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include software and application upgrades, additional preventive and detection measures, and enhanced process and technical controls.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The IHiS Board has appointed an independent human resource (HR) panel to examine the roles, responsibilities and actions of specific individuals involved and recommend the appropriate actions to be taken.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The panel was chaired by an IHiS Board member and comprised two other members from the public and private sectors with relevant HR and IT expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In assessing the appropriate HR actions, the panel considered whether the officers had acted in accordance with their job responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It also considered whether the officers’ action or inaction had contributed directly or indirectly to the outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The panel has submitted its recommendations to the IHiS Board and the Board released its decision on this matter yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To recap, two IHiS staff – the Team Lead of the Citrix Team and the Security Incident Response Manager – were found to be negligent and non-compliant with orders.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While the Citrix Team Lead had the necessary technical competencies, his attitude and approach to management of the servers introduced unnecessary and significant risks to the system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He could have mitigated the impact of the attack if he had enforced proper compliance and exercised effective management of the servers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Security Incident Response Manager persistently held a mistaken understanding of what constituted a "security incident" and when a security incident should be reported.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: His passiveness even after repeated alerts by his staff resulted in missed opportunities which could have averted or mitigated the impact of the cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Their behaviour had significant security implications and contributed to the unprecedented scale of the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Financial penalties were imposed on the two middle management supervisors who are accountable as supervisors of the staff that were terminated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A Cluster ISO was found to have a wrong understanding of what constituted a "security incident" and failed to comply with IHiS’ incident reporting procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Board decided to demote the Cluster ISO and reassign him to another role.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As the senior management team, they hold collective leadership responsibility over the organisation and the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IHiS CEO wrote a letter to me in December.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In his letter, he expressed disappointment that he and his IHiS colleagues were not able to prevent or respond better to the cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He and members of his senior management team acknowledged their collective responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The CEO expressed that he would accept whatever the IHiS Board may decide for him.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I have emphasised to the IHIS CEO and his senior management team to learn from this episode and lead the organisation and its staff through the recovery and rebuilding.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I expect them to do their utmost to remedy the shortcomings and help the public healthcare family emerge stronger, so as to win back public trust.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH and the rest of the public healthcare family will render them our full support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The COI did not identify lapses in specific individuals that are employed by SingHealth.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, SingHealth recognises its duty to its patients and its responsibility as the owner of the database system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The SingHealth senior leadership, including the Group CEO, has volunteered for a financial penalty which the Board has accepted.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Earlier, Minister Iswaran had shared that PDPC has completed its investigations into the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is the highest penalty meted out by PDPC to date.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IHiS and SingHealth have accepted PDPC’s decision and penalties.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They were proactive and demonstrated resourcefulness in managing the cyberattack.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The IHiS Board has presented Letters of Commendation to three IHiS staff from the Database Management Team, SCM Production Support Team and Security Management Team respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Each of them showed commitment to serve and had the persistence to get to the bottom of things.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am glad that their contributions have been recognised.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I would also like to acknowledge members of our public healthcare family who have worked hard together to ensure patient care is not compromised by this incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, I thank Singaporeans for their patience and understanding on the inconveniences they may have encountered at our public healthcare institutions arising from the implementation of tighter cybersecurity measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The public healthcare family will ensure that priority and attention are given to the implementation of COI’s recommendations as well as the cybersecurity initiatives that the public healthcare system has embarked on.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are organising our efforts into six key workstreams spanning technical measures, cybersecurity policy, organisational structures, governance enhancements, management of CII and patient engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we must not allow it to hold back our push towards using technology to provide better care for our patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: IT systems have improved the safety and effectiveness of patient care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It remains a key enabler we cannot do without for better delivery of healthcare to benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will not be a one-off exercise as new and evolving threats will continue to target our systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must continually fortify our defences, and we need a strong team working together to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We in the public healthcare family will take guidance from the COI report and strengthen our systems and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must and we will emerge with stronger cyber defences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will be the most fitting way to fulfil our responsibilities to our patients.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Speaker, Sir, I have a supplementary question for the Minister for Communications and Information.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I recall that he talked about three parallel investigations: the COI, the PDPC as well as the Police.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Any update on the last of these, whether there are any criminal findings?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Recommendation 4 of the COI states "enhanced security checks must be performed, especially on CII systems." My question is, what is the accountability mechanism for this?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Essentially, who will regulate cybersecurity officers to ensure such checks are up to a professional standard and performed regularly?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, what is the professional standard we are pegging the expectation to and how regularly will security checks be undertaken?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And, in that regard, CSA issues various directives and advisories from time to time.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And also, the audit will be conducted by an auditor that must be approved by CSA.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I pointed out, these have all been enabled with the legislation that came into force in August last year and, now, in having designated the CII, CSA is operationalising it and we have a mechanism to follow through on the broader imperatives that CSA has mapped out and also on the implementation of some of the COI recommendations.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: On the issue of ISS, it is encouraging that we are exploring the Virtual Browser option.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: But at the same time, during the exercise of ISS, I wonder whether there were instances of healthcare workers using their personal devices and data plans to access the Internet for work purposes and whether such practices introduced security risks and if, in future, there will be safeguards to caution our healthcare workers against these kinds of actions?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Indeed, some of the healthcare professionals have taken the initiatives to use their own personal devices to access Internet for work.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because their personal devices are not connected to the intranet, to our database system and, therefore, they are less risky from the systems point of view.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Whereas our own internal intranet system – we have imposed ISS on our own internal system and, therefore, our internal system will have no access to the Internet for surfing purposes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Speaker, I have a question for the Minister for Communications and Information.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate that the cybersecurity regime and ecosystem are a fairly relatively new frontier.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am just wondering, as part of our review and assessments, whether we look to the practices and systems in other countries and whether we benchmark ourselves against the technological capabilities as well as rigour and practices in those countries?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Obviously, because it is a highly interconnected world that we live in, in a sense, while we do what we can in our own jurisdiction, we also have to take reference from what is happening elsewhere.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Indeed, that is why cybersecurity agencies across the world formed these partnerships to share information and also to share best practices because the threat is an evolving one.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that is the way we continue to ensure that we are plugged in.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the short answer to the Member's question is yes, we do.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But having said that, the onus is on us to ensure that we are up to the mark, and I would add that many countries look to Singapore for best practices.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But the one elephant in the room, of course, is the decision that was made not to name the perpetrator.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: First of all, what actions, if any, can be taken against the perpetrators of such attacks?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And if the answer to this is "none at the moment", can we change our domestic laws at least, so that if any of these perpetrators are within our jurisdiction, we can take action against them?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I also want to echo my thanks to both Ministers and also to the COI for their work.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, while we are trying to strengthen the systems, if we take a leaf from how we manage infectious diseases while we are trying to think of better treatments and so on, I think a key focus would be surveillance, that means detection and containment.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, there was some talk about the advanced threat protection and other systems to detect the systems and, as I know it, our healthcare system has hundreds of computer systems, not just in SingHealth but also the private sector.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could I just ask what is the extent to which these detection systems have been deployed through the national healthcare system, just to get an idea?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because there are other healthcare systems out there that could still be vulnerable and may not have these systems.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I just want to have an idea about that.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, there was a point in the COI which merits study, which is the impact on patient care.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can I also find out what has been the work of MOH in looking at the impact that this cyberattack has had on patient care efficacy and efficiency?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, I am also concerned about the impact on the rollout of NEHR.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think it is something that we should all have.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is for the future of Singapore's healthcare.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, in terms of the study on NEHR, could I get a sense of what sort of goals we are looking at in terms of the assessment of whether or not NEHR will be safe in terms of cybersecurity threats and so on, so that maybe we have an idea how long this may be delayed?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is there to help us detect potential malicious activities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But for the private sector, it is something that we will have to work with them and see what would be applicable for them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is also important for us to always remember that whatever system we put in, there will always be the risk of exposure.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The greatest risk for us is to assume that after putting in Advanced Threat Protection or ISS, we are quite safe and, therefore, we let our guard down.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is, you must always be on alert and assume that we are being attacked all the time and be vigilant and get to know what is the latest development, what is the latest landscape, and continually upgrade ourselves to make sure that we are ready for them as best we can.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, this is a lesson we learnt from this incident.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu also asked about the impact due to this incident.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some patient care, some processes have been slowed down because of additional steps that they have to go through.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But by and large, we have not compromised the quality of care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And particularly on patient safety, we have been quite conscious about this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I have always reminded our cluster leadership to make sure that despite all the additional cybersecurity measures, we cannot compromise our patient safety.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So far, I think it has been going on all right.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On NEHR, I agree with Dr Chia Shi-Lu that we do not want to delay it unnecessarily.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is an indicative timeline and we will probably give an update nearer the time.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Speaker, Sir, I have a question for the hon Minister for Health in relation to the relationship between IHiS and SingHealth and, for that matter, the other healthcare clusters.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I note that PDPC had fined SingHealth in its capacity as a data controller.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But IHiS, which is owned by MOH Holdings (MOHH), is a nominated agency to deal with IT matters for all healthcare clusters.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, how would these two entities work to strike a balance between operational needs on the one hand and to maintain cybersecurity on the other hand?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Do they work as equal partners, or would there be another arbiter to deal with any differences between these agencies?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, he may be a secondee from IHiS, he may be a direct recruit, he may be someone that is loaned to the cluster, but his responsibility and accountability is towards the cluster.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, this provides the cluster some independence from IHiS as a system operator.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, security and operations now have separate reporting lines, and this provides significant independence between security considerations as well as operational requirements.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And this will also be quite separate from IHiS' Cyber Defence Group.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think the separation of roles among these few key functions will provide greater independence and check and balance between operational needs and cybersecurity needs.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The public version of the COI report is comprehensive on the technical facts of the cyberattack and also recommendations to prevent a repeat of such an incident.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But it has fallen short on the damage control for the victims of the cyberattack.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: To summarise, what is the Government going to do next to assure and alert this group of victims about such a danger?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Because telling the victim to make a Police report is rather moot after they have suffered financial/privacy loss because it is very difficult to investigate cross-border cybercrimes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because the way some of these scams, as the Member put it, are being perpetuated, is not just depending on this particular kind of incident.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They are approaching it from different angles, using different resources at their disposal.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, on the one hand, we are doing everything we can in taking it absolutely seriously that this has been an incident that we should not have allowed to happen.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But it having happened, we want to contain it and ensure that every measure is put in place to protect the interests of the patients.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if Members recall, SingHealth has made an extensive outreach to all the patients through SMSes and so on to inform them and also to advise them of the risks and what they need to do and why they can be assured in terms of the security of their data.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The second point I would make is, we have been emphasising, not just CSA, but the Government as a whole, whether it is this incident or any others, we have, each and every one of us, an obligation to exercise appropriate cyber hygiene habits.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that means if you have an unsolicited call seeking personal data, then our antenna should go up and we should be taking appropriate steps to ensure that this is a bona fide approach and not something that is a scam that is trying to take advantage of us.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Thirdly, we have, in general, an important and repeated advisory on appropriate cyber hygiene habits that should be undertaken by all of us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I do not know whether they are union members.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And if they are, it would be useful for the management to keep them informed.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And if they have not done so, it is still not too late.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Better to do now than not to do so at all.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think other than those I mentioned as part of the disciplinary action, the rest of the staff should not be affected.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Will MOH also assist private practitioners in coping with this cyberattack, especially those who are already embarking on NEHR?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: My concern is that cyberattacks on NEHR in the private sector may be linked to the public sector's.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: So, if there is a soft part in this area, will that affect the whole public sector in the end?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I would also like to echo Dr Chia Shi-Lu's question earlier whether the Minister will ensure that the NEHR is robust before it is widely implemented, to give confidence to patients and doctors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Lily Neo also mentioned how we can help private sector doctors, particularly if they are connected to NEHR.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we will also be developing advisories to help advise our private practitioners how to strengthen their system, how to do audits on their system to ensure that their own systems are protected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We must remember that even without NEHR, many of our doctors have their own data system and keep their own patient records.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Of course, these are limited to their own patients, not national data.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Nevertheless, it is also important for our private doctors to ensure that the patient data that they collect and maintain are protected from potential cyberattacks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In the past, our doctors may be using paper and pen, they have paper card records, it is less risky.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But still, the sense of responsibility to safekeep these data is there among our medical practitioners.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think it is no different when it comes to electronic records.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When doctors have their records kept in an electronic form, they should be quite mindful that they are also responsible to ensure that such electronic records within their own premises where they are kept, they also have to ensure that they are protected to a satisfactory extent.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will give them advice from time to time, especially arising from this incident.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will give them general advice on what they ought to do to ensure that their databases are protected.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: While we understand that there are deficiencies and they will be implementing comprehensive recommendations, we must not forget that our IHiS staff have been working very hard and performing their best over the years as we move towards a Smart Nation.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: So, can I ask what are the resources – as we are piling them up with more recommendations and more work – as well as emotional support that we are rendering to these ground IHiS staff while they are going through this trying period, to boost their morale as we learn and move forward stronger together in this Smart Nation journey?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On top of that, there are still many systems that they have to deliver and they have to deliver them with strong cybersecurity measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I would like to thank the Member for her encouragement, and will convey this to the IHiS team and to encourage them to press on with our task.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: It seems that the COI process has been very robust.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: It has been thorough, rigorous, public, transparent, and open.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: This will go some way to restore public confidence from the incident itself.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: I am sure the Government's position was well-calibrated and considered, but perhaps the Minister can share more on the considerations of the Government for not revealing who the perpetrator is.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The basic question we have to ask ourselves is how do we ensure that Singaporeans continue to have trust and confidence in our public sector systems – IT systems and databases – because it is inevitable that when you have an incident like this, it will raise such qualms and questions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I would say that in deriving a sense of confidence, our citizens should be looking at the totality of our response and not focus on one particular aspect of the response.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because they enable all these services, conveniences that we take for granted, whether it is in our transportation system, our healthcare system, in our dealings with various other Government agencies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The fact that we can transact with ease and convenience is because it is enabled by data and the IT systems that we have.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, firstly, we are doing this because we want to serve the interests of our citizens.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The second point I would make is that, directly as a result of this, we should be looking at what has our response been, the Government's response to this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because we want to demonstrate that we are transparent and we want to ensure that all Singaporeans understand that we have nothing to hide here.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We want to get to the bottom of it as much as Singaporeans do.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The only parts that have been held back are those that pertain to sensitive national security matters and also patient confidentiality.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Everything else is out there – unvarnished, stark but very clear on what we need to get done.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, again, if Members contrast what we have done with the responses in other domains by different parties, I think we can hold ourselves up to the best practices and standards in terms of how we responded.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Apart from action against individuals, we have taken actions against the organisations and we have also undertaken a slew of activities and measures in order to further strengthen our cybersecurity system, some informed by the COI, others that our agencies have already been working on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I do not think we should reduce whether we have confidence in the sense of justice to just one specific point, that there is no public attribution of the perpetrator.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources.
